instruction_text: Speak directly to one listener with warmth and a smile in your voice; calm, steady and reassuring, like a favorite morning radio host, while keeping the news clear and credible.
asr_text: I am for a rule at my daughter's high school. It would keep phones off during breaks and lunch too. Only banning them in class is not enough. I get home late from the job site. Fighting about phones every night makes me tired. If I can say, it's the school rule too, I won't be the only bad guy. My daughter did not keep our agreement. She was supposed to put her phone in the charging basket in the living room. I took her phone away. The next morning, it was hard to talk to her at breakfast. She also said, if I am the only one who replies late, I will be left out. I had no answer. I want her to keep our promise. I don't want to shout like my father either. But if she can't use her phone at school, nothing changes at home at night. Maybe I just want the school to help so my life is easier. I am a site supervisor who can't even manage things at home.
